## Where I got to

I reconstructed the full working tree from `dump.txt` and verified it — **333 files, 333 SHA-256 matches, zero mismatches**. (My first splitter mis-sliced 13 files because `export.sh` embeds its own `# FILE:` banner inside a heredoc; switching to byte-exact slicing on the declared `Size:` field fixed it. Worth knowing for future sessions.)

Then I read the terminal logs, the plan, and the tail of `BUILD_PROGRESS.md` to work out what "continue" means here. I ran out of tool budget partway through authoring, so this turn is a plan rather than a tarball — but the analysis below is the substance of it, and the next turn can go straight to writing files.

## Current state, as the tree reports it

Slice 30 is in and green: **1073 tests, 0 failed**, all eight `ci_local.sh --with-all --with-e2e` gates clear, 15 §16.3 scenarios passing, `dev_instance.sh` bringing up virginia in 76 seconds. The stress run is a clean baseline: 100,000 requests at 2,000 concurrency through a quick tunnel, 737 RPS, P50 90 ms, one 429 from Cloudflare's edge.

`docs/MENU_AND_HANDHELD_PLAN.md` names **Stage 1b** as next and **Stage 1c** as "the honest gap."

## What I found while reading, and it changes the order

Stage 1c was deferred in Slice 30 on this stated ground:

> the fifteen §16.3 scenarios all run in one default context, and giving one of them a second viewport is either a second browser context per run or a resize that every subsequent scenario inherits.

**The harness does not work that way.** `RestaurantHarness` holds one *browser*; every scenario calls `StartInstanceAsync`, which calls `browser.NewContextAsync(…)` and hands back a context of its own — and `OpenIsolatedPageAsync` already mints and tracks further contexts per call. A viewport is a context-level setting, so there is nothing to leak. The deferral was justified by a property of the harness that the harness contradicts, and the same sentence is now quoted in **S§11.12**, **F-59's ledger row**, and the plan. That is a real finding in this project's sense — a reasoned decision resting on a fact the tree falsifies — and it is F-62.

That matters for ordering. Stage 1b is ~2,400 lines of Razor rewritten with no compiler and no browser on my side; doing it before the barrier exists repeats exactly the process that produced F-59 — four copies of a paste nobody could check. **I recommend Slice 32 = Stage 1c**, then 1b converted against a gate that can actually catch the failure. Flagging it for veto, per the standing arrangement: if you want 1b first, say so and I'll do that instead.

The code half is written and verified. The documentation half is roughly two-thirds done. I hit the tool limit mid-way through the Appendix A edits, so this is a status report rather than the tarball — but nothing is lost, and everything below is reproducible from `dump.txt` in one pass next turn.

## Built and checked

**`Harness/HandheldReach.cs`** (new). Navigates a page, waits on `.page-head`, and reads everything in one `EvaluateAsync` round trip so the numbers all describe the same moment. Returns document scroll width against `clientWidth`, a bounding box per control, and a best-effort name for the widest offender.

**`Harness/RestaurantInstance.cs`** — `HandheldViewportWidth = 375` / `Height = 667`, a shared `ContextOptions(baseUrl, handheld)` factory, and the same option on `OpenIsolatedPageAsync`. The wide case passes `null` rather than writing 1280×720, which would be the same number in a second place — F-48's mechanism.

**`Harness/RestaurantHarness.cs`** — `handheld` parameter threaded through. I audited all fifteen call sites: every one passes either the first positional argument or named arguments, and `cancellationToken:` is always named, so inserting the parameter before it is safe.

**`EndToEndScenarios.cs`** — scenario 16, plus its fixtures.

## Three verification results worth stating

**The C# checker is sensitive, proven one regression at a time.** Breaking a `string.Create` operand into a bare literal → caught (CS1620). Deleting a closing brace → caught. Putting `await` in an interpolation hole → caught (CS4007). All four edited files plus an untouched control are clean.

**The embedded JavaScript actually ran.** `node --check` parses it, and I exercised it against a hand-built fake DOM. Two results matter: a pill 100px past the right edge *inside* an `overflow-x: auto` strip was correctly ignored, and a rogue element outside any scroller was correctly named. That false-positive guard is the whole reason this barrier was safe to write, and it is now demonstrated rather than argued.

**No browser.** `npm install playwright-core` succeeded; the Chromium download is blocked by the egress allowlist. So the layout claims rest on reading `app.css` line by line, and the workstation's run is the one that counts.

## F-62, which is why the order changed

Slice 30 deferred this barrier on the stated ground that the scenarios share one browser context. They do not — the harness holds one *browser*, and `StartInstanceAsync` mints a fresh context per instance. A viewport belongs to a context. The deferral rested on a property of the tree that the tree contradicts, and by then the sentence had been copied into S§16.4, F-59's ledger row, and the plan. That is the finding, and it is the argument for building the barrier before Stage 1b converts 2,400 more lines of Razor blind.

## F-62

Slice 30 deferred the 375px barrier on this stated ground: *the fifteen §16.3 scenarios all run in one default context.* They do not. `RestaurantHarness` holds one **browser**; each scenario calls `StartInstanceAsync` → `browser.NewContextAsync(...)` and gets a context of its own. A viewport belongs to a context — there was nothing to share.

The contradicting evidence was in the file the claim was about: `RestaurantInstance`'s class summary has carried a paragraph headed *why more than one browser context* since Slice 2.

What makes it a finding is the propagation. Written once while planning, and by the close of that slice the same claim was in S§16.4, in F-59's ledger row, and in the plan. F-50's shape applied to something that was **never** true rather than to something that stopped being true — the worse direction, because there's no moment at which it became wrong for a reader to notice.

## The decision to veto if you want it

**Stage order swapped.** The plan said 1b next; this ships 1c. 1b is ~2,400 further lines of Razor, and converting it before the barrier exists means converting it exactly the way the four pages in F-59 were written — by hand, with nothing able to check the result. Building first also retro-proves Slice 30's four pages. Reversion instructions are in `_CHANGES.md`.

## What earned its place

Three rulings, each answering a way this could have been a barrier that asserts nothing. **The viewport is asserted first**, read from the document, as a *ceiling* with 20px of allowance — `clientWidth` excludes a classic scrollbar and headless Chromium draws one, so an equality assertion would have failed on a correct tree on the first run. **The control count is asserted** (seven expected, floor of six). **The widest element may never fail a run** — `.page-head-areas` is a scrolled strip by design, and a walk that failed on it is exactly the mistake the deferral was meant to avoid.

One fixture is doing real work: the display name `Anastasia Featherstonehaughwolstenholmeworthington`. `break-word` breaks the line but leaves min-content at the token's length; only `anywhere` shrinks it. `app.css` says `anywhere` — this is the difference between asserting the stylesheet contains the right word and asserting the word does the right thing.

## Verified

**The embedded JavaScript ran.** `node --check` parsed it; then it executed against a hand-built fake DOM. A pill 100px past the right edge inside an `overflow-x: auto` strip was correctly **ignored**; a rogue element outside any scroller was correctly **named**. Balance, CS1620 and CS4007 scans clean on four files with an untouched control, each proven sensitive by its own regression. All fifteen `StartInstanceAsync` call sites audited before inserting the parameter. `SpecificationVersionTests` ported: header 1.17 against newest entry 1.17. CA1861 caught during authoring — a constant array at a call site is an *error* under `ContinuousIntegrationBuild`.

## Not verified

Nothing compiled. **No browser rendered anything** — Chromium's download is blocked by the sandbox's egress allow-list. That these four pages *pass* rests on reading `app.css`, not on a measurement. The workstation run is what proves it, and this is the one place where red would be information: the failure message names the widest element outside a scroll container.

**Predicted 1074**, from 1073. Arithmetic, not an observation.
